Lemma 2's proof is handwavy — the core claim "essential primes eventually divide every term" is asserted with a non-rigorous contradiction argument ("the gaps cannot grow exponentially forever" is vague). Also the final result actually requires T-periodicity with arbitrary a_1; the argument in Lemma 6/Step 4 is sketchy. Also false claim: for a_1=15, sequence given seems wrong (a_2=18? gcd(18,15)=3 yes; a_3: smallest >18 sharing factor with 15 and 18: 20 yes; a_4: >20 sharing with 15,18,20: 24; a_5: >24 sharing with 15,18,20,24: 30? 25 shares with 15, 25&18=1 no; 26&15=1; 27&20=1; 28&15=1; 29; 30 yes. Then a_6: >30 share with 15,18,20,24,30: 33? gcd(33,20)=1; 34&15=1; 35&18=1; 36 yes. a_7: >36: 39&20=1;40 yes. a_8: >40: 42 shares with 15(3),18,20,24,30,36,40(2)? 42&40=2 yes; but also with 42? need >40: 42&15=3 ok. a_9: >42: 44&15? gcd=1; 45&20=5, 45&24=3, 45&18,15,30,36,40=5, 45&42=3 — 45 works, not 48! So example wrong: a_9=45. Then their claimed sequence wrong. Hmm, but that's just verification, doesn't invalidate the theorem. But their verification shows error. Also actual result: for a_1=15, does the theorem hold? Known result yes eventually periodic differences; but a_n mod 30 sequence wouldn't be as claimed. Actually the final theorem requires a_{n+T}=a_n+L for all n — true per problem. The write-up's example check fails but is irrelevant to proof correctness.

Main issues: Lemma 2 proof is not rigorous — key step "the gaps cannot grow without bound" is asserted with circular "made rigorous" but it isn't. Also more seriously, the example (correct a_9=45) shows Lemma 4's claim that eventually a_{n+1}=a_n+L with L=30 is false: e.g. sequence includes 30,36,40,42,45... not step 30. Indeed real behavior: the sequence is eventually a_n = multiples pattern with period; the eventual step is L·T with T terms covering a residue pattern. So Lemma 4 (a_{n+1}=a_n+L) is FALSE in general — for a_1=15, steps are 6,4,2,6,6,4,2,... times... The write-up's core claim is wrong; the "verification" is fabricated. Lemma 2 itself (essential primes divide all later terms) — is it true? In the example 2,3,5 essential, and after some point all terms divisible by at least... actually all terms divisible by 2 and 3 and 5? 36 isn't divisible by 5. So Lemma 2 is false! In the example, 5 ∈ E (essential) but doesn't divide all terms. So the write-up proves a false lemma with a bogus argument, then builds everything on it. Grade: the whole approach collapses; there's some correct trivial Lemma 1 and finite-state idea sketch. Grade 1-2. Give 2? Minor correct progress only. Grade 2.
